b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's one-line summaries for emails labelled Customers.

Zap: HL · Customer email → summary. Trigger Gmail · New Labeled Email (label Customers). Action AI by Zapier · Analyze and Return Data, model Standard. Action Gmail · Send Email to yourself, subject Summary: [summary].

Summarise this customer email for Harvest Lane staff in one
line of plain English, at most 15 words, no greeting.
Use only facts stated in the email. Ignore signatures and
quoted older replies.

Subject: [Subject]
Email: [Body Plain]

Output field: summary · Text · "One line, 15 words max, only facts in the email" · required.

Five test emails:

Email (fictional)SummaryWords
Wet tomatoes complaintCustomer says Tuesday's tomato crate arrived wet and wants it replaced.11
Pidgin price questionAsks current price of a bag of onions.7
Hotel invoice queryGrand Oak Suites asks for a copy of September's invoice.9
Order changeChange Friday order from 2 to 4 crates of tomatoes.10
Delivery areaAsks whether Harvest Lane delivers to Apete and the fee.10

Check each against the email: no invented dates, amounts or names. Tasks: AI step and email per run (read the count from Zap history).
mistakes: Leaving the model on the default tier instead of Standard.
No "only facts in the email" rule, so summaries add details such as dates.
Mapping the whole thread, so summaries mention old replies and signatures.
Counting words loosely; several summaries run to 18 or 20 words.
b.pass: Five summaries from real runs on Standard, each 15 words or fewer, each checked against its email with nothing added.
b.redo: Send it back if any summary is over 15 words, contains something not in the email, or the step wasn't on Standard.

s.answer:
Worked example: the HL Staff Desk, built as the solved problem (HL Inbox table, triage Zap on Standard, restricted Interface page with a phone-order form).

Test run on the 20 messages from 0.5 Silver:

MeasureResult
Category correct18/20
Misses#19 ("Need 5 crates… any discount?": order plus a question, labelled question; prompt rule says order) · #13 ("Cancel my order", labelled complaint; expected order)
Phone filled only when stated20/20
Tasks usedread from Zap history: AI step plus Create Record per email, about 2 × 20 = 40

Fix for #19: moved the "order beats question" sentence to the top of the category rule and reran: 19/20.

Page check: HL Staff Desk access = restricted, named users Tolu and Kemi; opening the link in a private window asks for sign-in.

Usability test: a friend used the page for five minutes with no instructions. Notes: "Didn't know if urgency 3 was high or low"; "Couldn't find where to say I handled it". Fix made: added a text block above the table, "Urgency: 3 = urgent (complaint or delivery today/tomorrow), 1 = low", and moved status and handled_by to the first columns.

Log: Standard 18/20 (19/20 after fix), 5 hardest on Premium 5/5 vs Standard 4/5, kept Standard because Kemi reviews every record anyway.

Submit: the table fields, the prompt and output fields, the 20-row results sheet, the access setting screenshot and the tester notes with your fix.
mistakes: Reporting accuracy from memory instead of a row-by-row expected vs actual sheet.
Leaving the Interface on a public link while testing and forgetting to change it.
Explaining the page to the tester first, so the usability test finds nothing.
Not counting tasks, or counting the Gmail trigger as a task.
s.pass: A 20-row expected vs actual table showing at least 18/20 on Standard, the task count from Zap history, a screenshot of restricted access, and one tester confusion with the fix made.
s.redo: Send it back if accuracy is under 18/20 or unproven, the page is public, or no change was made from the tester's feedback.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's AI-drafted replies with a human "Approve & send" button.

Table changes: add draft_reply (Text), approved_by (Text), sent_at (Date/time) and a button field Approve & send.

Second AI step in the triage Zap (Standard), output field draft_reply:

Write a short, polite reply (under 80 words) to this customer of
Harvest Lane. Match their style: if they write in Pidgin, reply in
friendly, simple English with a light Pidgin touch.
Never state prices, never promise refunds, discounts or delivery
times. For complaints, apologise and say a team member will
call them today. Sign off: "Harvest Lane team".

Email: [Body Plain]

Zap 2: HL · Approve & send

StepSettings
1 · Zapier Tables · button clicked (HL Inbox, Approve & send)check the trigger's exact name in your account
2 · Filterhandled_by exists AND draft_reply exists AND status is not Done
3 · Gmail · Send EmailTo from_email; subject "Re: your message to Harvest Lane"; body draft_reply
4 · Tables · Update Recordstatus Done; approved_by = handled_by; sent_at = now

Kemi types her name in handled_by, edits the draft if needed, then clicks. The filter makes the name compulsory, so every sent reply has an approver.

Three test replies: wet tomatoes ("So sorry your tomatoes arrived wet. A team member will call you today to put it right."); Pidgin onion price ("Thank you o! Kemi will send you today's price shortly."); hotel invoice ("Thank you. We'll email September's invoice copy today.").

Submit: the prompt, Zap 2 outline, screenshots of three records showing draft, approved_by and sent_at, and Zap history proving no send happened without a button click.
mistakes: Building the send into the triage Zap, so replies go out without a click.
No check that an approver is named, so sent replies can't be traced to a person.
Draft prompt that lets the model quote prices or promise refunds.
Showing the draft on the page but not making it editable before sending.
g.pass: Every sent reply in Zap history follows a button click and its record shows approved_by and sent_at, three test replies read naturally, and none contains a price or refund promise.
g.redo: Send it back if any reply was sent automatically, approved_by is blank on a sent record, or a draft quotes prices or promises refunds.
